newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Telstra says to start talks on WorldPartners stake.
newsitem.headline: Telstra says to start talks on WorldPartners stake.

text.p: Australia's state-owned telecommunications company Telstra Corp said on Monday it has signed a memorandum of understanding to begin talks on taking a stake in global telecommunications alliance WorldPartners Co.
Telstra said the agreement with WorldPartners did not affect Telstra's ownership, nor did it impact on the services offered to most Australians.

"Under the alliance, we will ensure our networks are compatible, and that we offer compatible and innovative products to our customers, and the customers of other carriers in the alliance," said retail products director Lindsay Yellard.
WorldPartners are AT&T Corp, Singapore Telecom, Kokusai Denshin Denwa (KDD) Ltd of Japan, the Unisource joint venture of Europe.

"There is no doubt the world's telecommunications market is becoming more competitive as governments around the globe rush to lower their regulatory barriers. Telstra needs to position itself to play a key role in this new environment," Yellard said.
Unisource is a venture owned by Koninklijke PTT Nederland (KPN) of the Netherlands, Telia of Sweden and Swiss Telecom PTT.
Worldpartners was formed in 1993 and has 17 international telecommunications operators as members in 33 countries.
